title: Statistical Machine Learning for Comparative Protein Dynamics with DROIDS/maxDemon
author: Babbitt, Fokoue, et al.

steps.title: Prepare PDB files for analysis
steps.instruction: Obtain the appropriate PDB structure(s) for the functional comparison you wish to study, clean and edit them to create the required files for DROIDS, and ensure they are formatted correctly for downstream MD simulation.

substeps.instruction: Find a PDB file representing the natural functional comparison (e.g., unbound vs. bound, orthologs, paralogs) or evolutionary comparison you intend to analyze.

If studying a protein‑ligand interaction, create and save three PDB files: (i) protein + ligand complex, (ii) protein alone, and (iii) ligand alone. Use molecular visualization software such as UCSF Chimera, UCSF ChimeraX, or PyMOL.
Clean each PDB file by removing all extraneous molecules (e.g., crystallization additives) and any x‑ray reflection records if present.

Verify that no post‑translational modifications (PTMs) are present that cannot be handled by the Amber protein force fields. If such PTMs are required for the study, remove them now and later add them back with appropriate software (e.g., https://glycam.org) using a compatible GLYCAM force field (e.g., GLYCAM_06j‑1, which works with Amber ff12, ff12SB and later).
Leave crystallographic water molecules in the file; they will be automatically removed during later MD preparation steps.

Do not manually add hydrogens; they will be added automatically later. Only add hydrogens manually if you plan to analyze a specific protonation state, and later you can choose to skip the automatic hydrogen‑addition step.

Open each PDB file in a plain‑text editor and delete all MODEL/ENDMDL records and any CONECT lines. Example lines to remove: "CONECT 1688 1711", "MODEL 2", "ATOM 1 O5' DC B 1 71.829 85.622 -69.018 1.00 62.33", "ENDMDL", etc.
If the file contains DNA, ensure protein residues are listed before nucleotides, then delete all TER lines belonging to DNA chains while keeping TER lines for protein chains.

Note the required number of files: for protein‑protein or protein‑RNA/DNA analyses you need only two PDB files (bound and unbound states); for protein‑ligand analyses you need three files as described above.

steps.title: Configure DROIDS analysis GUI
steps.instruction: Launch the DROIDS graphical user interface, set up software paths if needed, and select the desired type of comparative dynamics analysis.

substeps.instruction: Open the first DROIDS GUI window and specify the paths to the required software dependencies (Amber and UCSF ChimeraX). Save the control file; this step can be skipped if a control file for your computer already exists.

Proceed to the second GUI window, which presents three main analysis options: (i) simple statistical comparison of site‑wise dynamics, (ii) comparison of dynamics with introduced mutations, and (iii) site‑wise dynamics comparison followed by machine‑learning identification of conserved dynamics.

Choose the appropriate analysis type and then select the functional comparison category that matches your experiment (protein homologs, protein‑DNA interaction, protein‑small‑molecule ligand interaction, or protein‑protein interaction).
